title: CEO Interview with Mark Rushworth of Finchetto
gist: Finchetto's CEO pitches a fully optical packet switch that uses light to control light, modeled to cut latency 700x and power 20x versus electro-optical switches for a 48-port Ethernet design. Only a 4x4 discrete-component demonstrator exists so far; the next step is a ten-month TFLN photonic-chip manufacturing program in Cardiff.

insights.claim: Network switches account for as much as 10 percent of data center power, making the network a larger share of AI's energy bill than most people expect.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Networking power is an underappreciated AI energy line item that new switch tech targets.
insights.quote: Network switches are a power-hungry component of the data center, accounting for as much as 10 percent of its power.

insights.claim: In clustered AI training, an inadequate network leaves expensive GPUs idle while still drawing power, so network performance directly determines silicon utilization.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Network limits waste capex and power on accelerators, supporting spend on interconnect.

insights.claim: As link speeds move from 400 Gb/s to 800 Gb/s and toward 1.6 Tb/s, a switch that is marginal at 400 becomes a ceiling at 800, and electronic switches hit limits at that scale.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Electronic switching may become the binding constraint as link speeds climb.
insights.quote: a switch that is marginal at 400 becomes a ceiling at 800

insights.claim: Every electronic switch hop converts light to an electrical signal, reads the packet, and converts it back to light, so the latency floor does not move even as power dissipation grows.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Optical-electrical-optical conversion is the structural latency and power cost an all-optical switch removes.

insights.claim: Working around the switch with point-to-point links multiplies laser sources and drives power up nonlinearly.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Point-to-point workarounds are not a power-efficient alternative to better switching.
insights.locator: Building around it with point-to-point links

insights.claim: Finchetto is building what it calls the world's first fully optical network packet switch, moving data as light with no electrical conversion; a light-based control signal sent in parallel with the packet sets its route.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Defines the technical approach: light controlling light, nonlinear optics.
insights.quote: We’re building the world’s first fully optical network packet switch

insights.claim: Finchetto's 48-port Ethernet switch design is modeled to cut latency by 700x and power by 20x versus conventional electro-optical switches; these are modeled figures, not measured, with only a 4x4 demonstrator built.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Headline claims are simulated and unproven at scale; treat as early-stage.
insights.quote: modeled to cut latency by 700x and power by 20x

insights.claim: The company has a working 4x4 Ethernet demonstrator that switches at line rate.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Proof of physics exists, but at tiny port count.

insights.claim: Because the switch is passive, it is agnostic to line rate, so moving from 800 Gb/s to 1.6 Tb/s and beyond would not require replacing it, unlike electronic switches limited to the processor's design line rate.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Future-proofing across speed generations would be a TCO argument if it works.

insights.claim: The patented method uses nonlinear optics for switching rather than one narrow implementation, so it could extend to other networks and longer term to quantum-adjacent and optical compute systems.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Optionality claims beyond data centers are long-dated and speculative.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: An all-optical packet switch has no buffer memory and requires flow control to be handled differently from electronic networks, which the CEO acknowledges is a hard design challenge.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Absence of buffering is a key technical risk for adoption.
insights.locator: Designing an all-optical packet switch is hard

insights.claim: Optical circuit switches already on the market set up paths ahead of the data and rely on electronic control and software, whereas Finchetto decides per packet using light with no electronic control in the path.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Positions against existing optical switching incumbents, not just electronic ones.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: AI traffic patterns shift as workloads move between training and inference, so per-packet routing can follow traffic and spread load across a large fabric better than pre-planned paths.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Dynamic AI traffic is the argument for packet over circuit optical switching.
insights.locator: That matters for AI because the traffic does not sit still.

insights.claim: Incumbent competition in switching comes from electronic switches from Nvidia, Arista and Cisco.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Names the incumbents a successful optical switch would displace.
insights.quote: The incumbents are electronic switches from companies such as Nvidia, Arista and Cisco.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Prototypes use discrete optical components that are not cost-effective for mass manufacture, so Finchetto is moving to photonic integrated circuits and has started a ten-month program to establish a thin-film lithium niobate chip process at Cardiff University cleanrooms.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Manufacturability on TFLN is the next gating milestone.
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

insights.claim: The TFLN program is backed by an Investor Partnerships Programme grant and investment from Development Bank of Wales.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Funding is public-sector and modest in the disclosed detail.

insights.claim: Finchetto is designing for incremental adoption because no data center will rebuild around a new switch: it interoperates with existing transceivers, GPUs and protocols and drops into spine-and-leaf architectures.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Drop-in compatibility lowers adoption friction for novel network hardware.
insights.quote: No data center will rebuild around a new switch
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?

insights.claim: Packet-level switching requires a laser that can retune in nanoseconds; Pilot Photonics lasers were the fastest Finchetto found and are being designed into next-generation demonstrators.
insights.speaker: Mark Rushworth
insights.so_what: Fast tunable lasers are a critical supply dependency and partner opportunity.
